subject: k-pop fans
one_liner: Coworking for K-pop fans whose collections have moved out before they have.
brand_voice_notes: Deadpan coworking copy about a hobby acquiring rent, colleagues and a reception desk. Familiar setups: staying too long, collecting too much, and knowing online friends only by usernames. Explain collectible photo cards through what people do. Keep booking labels literal. The comic turns must work for someone outside the fandom.
demo_screen_concept: WeWork-like workspace booking for a K-pop clubhouse: date, six shared-desk controls with availability, Day pass / Resident / Private office tabs, optional screening-room duration, included minutes and live total. Confirm a $32 desk plus 45 screening minutes for $40; the desk becomes occupied and the receipt agrees. Monthly tabs preview actual entitlements without a purchase. Shared cobalt/pink identity, music-poster typography and a fan-space campaign banner establish the audience. Mailroom details reveal collection-v2.webp and a clearly labeled sample delivery of 24 albums. Keep the six-desk private-office overlay and all existing working booking behavior.

hero.sub: Coworking for K-pop fans. Book a desk, watch a three-minute video for two hours, and have the albums delivered somewhere your family can't count them.

features.title: Three minutes of music. Two hours of room hire.
features.blurb: Book a screening room for the new video. Watch it once for each singer, then again because someone blinked. You came here to get away from meetings. This one has a waiting list.

features.title: Your collection moved out before you did.
features.blurb: Have your albums delivered to reception. Take out the collectible photo cards and keep them. Leave the spare albums on your rented shelf. Your collection now has its own address. You still live with your parents.

features.title: Reception needs their actual names.
features.blurb: Send guest passes to the fan friends you talk to every day. Reception needs the names on their IDs. You've shared hotel rooms. You've lent them money. You're about to ask what their name is.

pricing_tiers.name: Day pass
pricing_tiers.tagline: You said this was a one-off.
perks: One available desk from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.
30 minutes in a screening room; additional time costs $8 per 15 minutes.
Two guest passes for photo-card trades at your desk.
Take every album home at closing. Yes, every copy.

pricing_tiers.name: Resident
perks: A dedicated desk with access seven days a week.
Two screening-room hours each month; additional time costs $8 per 15 minutes.
Reception accepts up to 20 parcels a month; one storage shelf holds the albums you're still finding homes for.
Ten guest passes each month for traders and group-order pickups.

pricing_tiers.name: Private office
pricing_tiers.tagline: Your fan club now pays commercial rent.
perks: A lockable office with six desks and six member keys.
Twelve screening-room hours each month; additional time costs $8 per 15 minutes.
Reception accepts up to 100 parcels a month; six storage shelves keep the corridor clear.
Fifty guest passes each month. Reception checks visitors against your pickup list.

testimonials.quote: I booked thirty minutes for the new video. We spent twenty arguing about who should sit nearest the screen. Then we pressed play.
testimonials.name: Priya Shah
testimonials.title: Release-watch organiser; payroll assistant

testimonials.quote: My mum said it was time to get my own place. The albums have their own place now. I'm still in my old room.
testimonials.name: Daniel Reyes
testimonials.title: Album collector; still living at home

testimonials.quote: Reception asked for my guest's surname. We've been on holiday together twice. I had to message her.
testimonials.name: Mina Park
testimonials.title: Fan-club member; junior designer

observations.behavior: Fans replay a short music video and discuss every performer.
observations.mechanic: Book a screening room with limited included minutes and paid extensions.
observations.consequence: Someone joins a coworking club to escape meetings and ends up in a two-hour meeting about a three-minute song.

observations.behavior: Collectors buy duplicate albums for small collectible cards and run out of space at home.
observations.mechanic: Rent shelf storage and use a staffed mailroom under a monthly workspace membership.
observations.consequence: The collection gets its own rented address before its owner can move out of their parents’ house.

observations.behavior: Online fan friends know each other intimately but use usernames.
observations.mechanic: Issue a guest pass with the visitor’s legal name for reception check-in.
observations.consequence: Friends who have shared holidays and lent money must ask each other their real names to enter the office.

source_product_patterns: Book an available desk on a workspace floor plan.
Choose between daily access, a dedicated desk and a private office.
Reserve shared rooms using included hours and paid extensions.
Receive deliveries at a staffed reception desk.
Assign storage space to a recurring membership.
Register visitors and issue a limited number of guest passes.
editorial_plan.composition_plan: Opening pairs oversized plain-language title with a live booking preview: date, desk D04, 30 included room minutes, two guest passes, $32 day rate and direct route to that desk. The booking card opens with a fan clubhouse campaign composition, followed by live reservation details. Three distinct human jokes lead into the album-storage illustration, member quotes and escalating memberships. Demo retains the WeWork-like date/space/room/receipt flow with audience-derived type, colors and artwork.

references.reference: K-pop physical album inserts and collectible photo-card sleeves
references.cues: Bold condensed type, pink translucent framing, cobalt album blocks, tangible printed collage.
references.application: Campaign imagery, title typography, member quote cards and pink booking frame.

references.reference: Fan-made concert merchandise and release-campaign posters
references.cues: Confident oversized lettering, ticket-like rules and music-release color blocking.

audience_design.landing_application: Album-inspired identity around a readable proposition and real desk/date/room booking preview. Two newly composed campaign assets show fan workspace and excess album storage. Avoid arbitrary decorative badge systems.
audience_design.demo_application: Keep date, desk availability, room duration and itemized reservation summary prominent. Apply shared condensed headings, pink borders and cobalt selection; retain the furnished floor plan as a practical workspace map.

design_direction.style: K-pop album-insert clubhouse: oversized condensed black type, cobalt bands, pink collectible-card framing and warm-white printed surfaces.

fonts.pairing: Oswald with DM Sans; condensed music-poster display and readable booking UI.

design_direction.archetype: Workspace membership landing with a usable booking preview, fan-club campaign strip, open feature passages and album-insert pricing.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 150ms color response to controls; no ambient motion. Respect reduced motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Large left-aligned proposition with right-hand fan-campaign artwork and a compact live reservation preview in one pink sleeve. Dates, desks, allowances and price remain live text. Shared type, color and image cues establish the audience at first glance.

items.prompt: Design the actual finished original brand logo for "Annex", a fictional coworking office for K-pop fans whose album orders and viewing parties now require rented space. Direction A: architectural adjoining-room symbol with a precise open doorway / door-swing detail; compact floor-plan silhouette containing one pale yellow occupied room. Bespoke confident geometric sans wordmark exactly "Annex" to its right. Drafting blue #285DB5 and graphite #252E36 with pale yellow #F2DA7E, on completely flat paper-white #F7F8F4. Make the symbol distinct and legible at 32px, thick enough lines. Clean flat graphic design, no presentation board, no mockup, no gradients, no shadow, no extra text, no trademark copies. Horizontal lockup centered with ample clear space, symbol isolated to left of wordmark. 3:2 image.
items.verdict: Direction A selected. Exact Annex spelling, balanced bold lettering and compact floor-plan silhouette. Cropped only outer blank margin; no redesigned geometry. Stronger than B at small size; thick perimeter remains legible.

items.prompt: Approved identity reference attached: preserve its blue architectural geometry and yellow occupied-area language. Design an editorial architectural composition, an overhead furnished office plan for Annex coworking space for K-pop fans. Rectangular footprint with generous white corridors: left open desk area with two paired bench tables and six chairs; upper right a screening room with projector, screen and four chairs; lower right a mailroom with shelves of albums, a trolley and reception counter. A small six-person private office along top. Architectural blue #285DB5 linework, graphite #252E36 detail, pale yellow #F2DA7E occupied room floors, paper-white #F7F8F4. Beautiful restrained axonometric furniture, precision line weights, sophisticated architectural prospectus composition, human-scale details like headphones, photocard binder and album stacks. Compose only these exact large readable labels: "Desks", "Screening room", "Mailroom", "Private office". No desk numbers, prices, other text or watermarks. No rendered software UI. Leave margins and preserve whole outer footprint. A complete designed architectural artwork, not a plain flowchart or photograph. Wide landscape 3:2.
items.placement: Demo floor plan with existing six-workstation overlay, retained as practical map.
items.verdict: The source illustration has four room labels and the accepted blue/yellow identity. Its private office contains two workstations. Both HTML pages correct that room with an identical responsive SVG layer, reusing six desk-and-chair crops from this same asset, retaining the surrounding rooms and adding a live six-desk/six-key caption. No asset pixels were modified. Numbered desk controls refer to the separate shared area.
items.export: Full composition preserved; deterministic RGB WebP conversion, no crop.

items.prompt: Approved identity reference attached: use its exact geometric blue architectural language. Create a composed information-design artwork for Annex, an office rented by K-pop fans. Axonometric cutaway mailroom cabinet and trolley, with one opened shipping carton, neatly repeating album copies arranged upright on shelves, and a small collectible portrait card removed from one album. The point: many copies are opened for collectible cards, spare albums take up rented storage. Beautiful architectural sectional illustration, deliberate asymmetric layout with 3 large textual anchors integrated into drawing, rich furniture detail and bold graphic negative space. Exact text ONLY: "24 albums", "Photo cards kept", "Shelf space used". Give 24 album spines in four groups of six, with one visibly opened album; a few tiny illustrated portrait cards above the shelf. Do not label the number of photo cards. Drafting blue #285DB5, pale yellow #F2DA7E, graphite #252E36, paper-white #F7F8F4. Blue linework, restrained pencil texture. Typography must be large and legible. No extra copy, watermarks, logos, software UI or photography. Full uncropped composition, landscape 3:2.
items.placement: Retained original asset, superseded in visible pages by collection-v2.webp.
items.verdict: Accepted: all three supplied labels spelled correctly, architectural cutaway and card extraction communicate why storage is rented. 24 is the sample delivery size; shelves are illustrative, not a literal spine-count chart. Large typography remains legible at mobile display size.
items.export: Full composition preserved; deterministic RGB WebP conversion, no crop.

items.prompt: Create a polished original graphic-design artwork for Annex, a fictional coworking club for K-pop fans. Landscape 3:2 editorial campaign collage combining a carefully art-directed dollhouse cutaway of a fan coworking space with K-pop album-package graphics. Warm white #FFFDF8, black #191919, saturated cobalt #285DB5, vivid pink #EE467A, pale pink #FFDCE8. Stylish clean contemporary Korean music merchandise aesthetic: physical album sleeves, collectible-card frames, translucent pink acrylic, bold condensed black typography, fine registration marks used sparingly. Show a real shared workspace with desk stations, music-video screening lounge with sofa and screen, and mailroom stacked with duplicate albums. Small stylized adult fans using the rooms, no recognizable celebrities, brands or trademarks. Furnished interior must clearly read as a modern coworking space, made personal by album posters and card binders. Embed exactly these three large well-composed typographic labels: "Desk space." "Fan business." "Annex". Beautiful asymmetric editorial composition, white negative space, sophisticated tangible paper and acrylic textures, cobalt room outlines. No software UI, charts, watermarks, gibberish or other text. No exact desk-count claims. This is a composed campaign illustration to support a real website, not a website screenshot.
items.placement: Landing opening booking card and demo member-space banner
items.verdict: Inspected at full resolution: requested wording legible, cobalt/pink family consistent, composition communicates fan workspace or disproportionate album storage. All essential claims are repeated in live HTML.
items.export: Full composition converted to WebP at quality 86, no crop or creative pixel edits.

items.prompt: Create a polished original graphic-design artwork for Annex, a fictional coworking club for K-pop fans. Landscape 3:2 designed editorial still-life collage about buying many copies of the same music album to find a small collectible photo card. K-pop album packaging and fan-merchandise art direction: warm white #FFFDF8, black #191919, cobalt #285DB5, vivid pink #EE467A, pale pink #FFDCE8, tangible paper, translucent acrylic, clean studio shadows, condensed bold black typography. Deliberate composition: one small portrait-format collectible card in a clear pink-edged sleeve at the upper left, connected through an artfully laid-out trail of repeated cobalt and pink fictional album boxes occupying large rented storage shelves across the right and bottom. Card depicts an invented adult musician, no real celebrity. The visual joke is the huge amount of album storage required to keep one little card. Only exact typography allowed, large and beautifully composed: "Keep the card." "Rent the shelf." "Annex". Frame and hierarchy like a premium music album insert, sophisticated physical collage and designed information illustration. No exact count of albums. No charts, software UI, watermarks, real trademarks or extra text.
items.placement: Landing collection feature and demo mailroom details
items.verdict: Inspected at full resolution: requested wording legible, cobalt/pink family consistent, composition communicates fan workspace or disproportionate album storage. All essential claims are repeated in live HTML.
items.export: Full composition converted to WebP at quality 86, no crop or creative pixel edits.

items.prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Design the final production logo for "Annex", a coworking club for K-pop fans. Input image is the approved campaign ART DIRECTION reference only. Create an original typographic wordmark consistent with the bold black italic condensed Annex lettering in the reference: confident, compact, forward leaning, carefully kerned, subtly custom cut terminals, unmistakable exact spelling "Annex". Make the capital A a strong recognizable silhouette suitable for a favicon crop. Black ink #191919 only, genuinely transparent background, no texture or shading. Wide horizontal wordmark, generous clear space all around, the word should occupy most of the width. The identity should look at home on a K-pop album sleeve and in the navigation of a serious workspace booking product. Render the actual finished high resolution flat logo only.
